purpose: Three speed-ups of high-MOI CRT runs for 1.6.0-dev.2, each byte-identical to dev.1: stored first-stage draws scored in cell-major form (legacy), and each response's score state and each target's propensity model kept across tiles. Alternatives, numbers, choices, reasons.
data: Gasperini et al. 2019, GEO GSE120861 (public); panel t100_g7418 (100 targets x 7,418 genes, 741,800 pairs), seed 20260930, cell_qc false.
host: uwt-biocloud1, Intel Xeon E5-2640 v4, 8 threads on cores 1-8, SMT siblings 11-18 idle, nothing else running
configuration: tiled as the full-set runs: legacy (reuse_draws, confirm_draws 0) in tiles of 64 targets x all responses (2 tiles); default in tiles of all targets x 256 responses (29 tiles); checkpoint_dir, phase all

extrapolation.method: Each item's CPU-time saving on the tiled panel, per unit of the work it removes, times that work in the full test set (1.5.0 AWS counts, validation/GASPERINI_FULL_CLOUD_1_5_0.json), subtracted from dev.1's modelled thread time (validation/BATCH_SCORING.json); the ratio is applied to dev.1's AWS-scaled hours.

1_cell_major_first_stage.design: With batch scoring and reuse_draws, the stored first-stage draws of consecutive targets are grouped by about 2,048 draws (4 targets of 499) and transposed once per run: per cell a 16-bit count and the 16-bit indices of the group's draws that contain it. A response whose pairs cover at least half of a group's targets scores the whole group in one pass over its records in cell order, adding each record to the sums of its draws (two 4-lane AVX2 adds per draw, or the scalar loop); the sums (128 KB) stay in the core's cache. Each draw adds its records in ascending cell order, so its sums and statistic are those of score_draws bit for bit. Later stages, partial groups and draws over the budget keep score_draws.
alternatives: score_draws (blocked, 32,768 cells, two draws at a time): 3.7 ns per treated cell and draw (8 threads)
cell-major groups of 2 / 4 / 8 targets: 3.8 / 2.7 / 3.3 ns (2: the records are read 50 times per response; 8: the sums leave the core's cache)

a group scored when at least half of its targets are scored for the response (chosen) or always (wasted passes for sparse pair lists, such as cis pairs) or only when complete (a target whose pair fails pair QC would drop its whole group back to score_draws)
32-bit counts per cell (0.8 MB per group) or 16-bit (chosen, 0.4 MB): a group has at most 65,535 draws
1_cell_major_first_stage.choice: groups of 2,048 draws (4 targets), at least half of a group's targets scored, 16-bit counts and indices
1_cell_major_first_stage.reason: 1.37 times faster kernel on 79% of the legacy draws, results unchanged; about 2.2 bytes per treated cell and draw more memory (55% of the stored first stage, within draw_cache_mb)

2_score_state_across_tiles.design: sceptre_tiled keeps, for each response, the inverse information and nuisance correction (the O(p^2) part of its BinaryScoreWorkspace) from the first tile that computes it (SceptreShard::score_states). Each tile builds the per-cell score records from the rebuilt null directly, without ScoreWorkspace's copies of the design, weights and residuals, its cross product and its inverse; the state uses ScoreWorkspace's checks and arithmetic, so the records are bit for bit the same.
alternatives: keep the whole score records across tiles: 13 MB per response, about 97 GB for 7,418 responses (rejected, memory)
keep the O(p^2) state (chosen): 42 doubles per response, about 2.5 MB in all
larger tiles (tile_targets 128 halves the rebuilds) at about 4.7 GB more stored draws per tile, and a changed default (not adopted)
persist the state in the checkpoint directory for tiles run as separate processes (not adopted: the full-set runs use one process; a resumed or separate process computes it again, with the same bits)
2_score_state_across_tiles.choice: the O(p^2) state in memory within one process
2_score_state_across_tiles.reason: removes the cross products and copies per response and tile at about 2.5 MB; the O(n) records and the null rebuild remain per tile

3_propensity_across_tiles.design: sceptre_tiled keeps each target's propensity status and coefficients from the first tile that fits it (SceptreShard::propensities); later tiles build the sampler from them. The fit is a deterministic function of the design and the target's labels, so the kept coefficients are the bits a refit gives.
alternatives: keep the samplers too: 12 bytes per cell and target, about 9.5 GB for 3,837 targets (rejected, memory)
keep the coefficients (chosen): O(p) per target, about 0.2 MB
fit propensities in the prepare phase and persist them (not adopted, as for item 2)
3_propensity_across_tiles.choice: coefficients in memory within one process
3_propensity_across_tiles.reason: removes 28 of 29 propensity fits per target in default-mode tiled runs; samplers are still built per tile (about 8.6 ms each)

memory.full_set_estimate: The kept data add about 1.1 MB per target in a legacy tile (64 targets: about 70 MB) and about 3 MB in all for the states of items 2 and 3. With the default-mode rise seen on the panel (0.3 to 0.4 GB at 8 threads), the full-set peaks (34.3 GB legacy, 42.1 GB default at 16 threads on 1.5.0) are expected to rise by under 1 GB.
memory.note: Legacy peaks are unchanged within 0.05 GB. Default-mode peaks rose from 11.19 / 11.31 GB to 11.58-11.66 GB with item 2, whose kept states take about 3 MB. The rise most likely follows the changed allocation of the score records (a BinaryScoreWorkspace built directly instead of inside a ResamplingWorkspace) in glibc's per-thread arenas rather than kept data; this was not investigated further.
